why: Prices are served strictly from high to low, so group bids by price and process groups in descending order; inside a group the one-at-a-time round robin can be simulated in bulk by giving everyone min(remaining request) per full round instead of share by share.
hints: Who gets served first is fixed by price, so sort or heap the price groups from highest to lowest.

Within a group, if the shares left cover every request, everybody is satisfied; otherwise round robin by timestamp means each bidder gets one share per round, and the first bidders in timestamp order get the leftovers.

Process groups until shares run out; a bidder is unallotted only if their group was never reached or the round robin ran out before their first share (k shares left, group of size g > k: the last g - k by timestamp get nothing). O(n log n).
pitfalls: Simulating one share at a time is too slow: totalShares can be 10^9.
In a tied group with fewer shares than bidders, only the earliest-timestamp bidders get a share.
A user who got even one share is not in the answer; return ids sorted ascending.
